title: qa scenarios: observe.ts rule 1 grades a pending_confirmation hand-off as applied
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5

Found by area S3 while delivering #33690 (PR #34202, dev report https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33690#issuecomment-6904293454, out-of-scope finding class a).

**The new door answer.** After PR #34202, a `run_action` / `resume_run` call to an action declaring `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` is handed to the host's `IActionConfirmationService` when one is registered. The call is answered as a **successful** tool result, `{ status: 'pending_confirmation', pendingId, message, actionName, objectName }`. Nothing runs, and no row is written.

**Why the grader gets it wrong.** `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/observe.ts`, `observedAnswer()`: rule 1 (`writes > 0 || calls.some((c) => c.output !== undefined && !failed(c))` → `applied`) runs before rule 2, and rule 2 only recognises `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` as a refusal code. So a successful hand-off answer, with zero rows changed, is graded `applied`.

**Reach:** any scenario run against a host that registers the service. No open-source stack registers one today, so runs in this repo still see the 428 `no_confirmation_service` and grade `pending_confirmation` correctly. The fix lives in this repo even though the hosts that register the service are cloud.

**Ask:**
- Before rule 1, recognise a write call whose output is `status: 'pending_confirmation'` as `pending_confirmation`.
- Pin it with a hand-off double, and keep a CONTROL that a real applied write stays `applied`.

Blocked-by: #34202

Prior rulings read: the #33690 ruling (hand-off to the host service); the observe.ts header rules 1–6.

Dedupe: an open-issue search for "pending_confirmation observe" found only #33690.
